After a long reign at the top of this list, Yesteryear has been pushed out of the top five by a new release! Can you guess what took its spot? Here are some hints: it’s a memoir, and the top Goodreads review describes it as “What if the worst friend you ever had became the most successful person in the world?”
But before we get into the most read books on Goodreads this week, let’s talk about some other new releases that should be on your radar.
Two New Books Out This Week You Should Know About
Unfortunately, the most read books on Goodreads tend not to be diverse by any definition of the word. So, here are a couple of new books out this week that deserve wider readership.
Two Can Play That Game by Zakiya N. Jamal

Last year, I was happy to spread the word about Zakiya Jamal’s two 2025 releases: her adult romance, Sparks Fly, and her YA romance, If We Were a Movie. Her latest adult release is a fake-dating sapphic sports romance about a rising influencer and a WNBA star who link up after a chance courtside encounter. What starts as a strategic partnership and image rehabilitation job soon takes a turn for the steamy. —Vanessa Diaz
Line of Descent by Adam Oyebanji

If you haven’t acquainted yourself with the novels of Adam Oyebanji, you should fix that now. He’s written a couple of great mysteries, and his sci-fi thrillers like Braking Day and Esperance are out of this world! This upcoming thriller is about a generation ship, the Archimedes, where a strange kidnapping leads to mystery and murder. —Liberty Hardy
The Most Read Books on Goodreads This Week
Daddy Issues: A Memoir by Sofia Franklyn

Sofia Franklyn was the co-creator of the popular podcast Call Her Daddy, but she left the show when she went through a very public friend breakup with her co-host. In her new memoir, which came out November 10th, she shares her side of the story. It was read by 22,000 users this week and has a 4.2 average rating.
Sunrise on the Reaping by Suzanne Collins

This prequel novel in the Hunger Games series was published in 2025, but it’s getting new interest ahead of the movie adaptation, which came out November 20th. It follows Haymitch’s Hunger Games, 24 years before the events of the first novel. It was read by almost 26,000 users this week and has a 4.5 average rating.

The fourth book in the Empyrean series still doesn’t have a release date, so fans likely have a long time to wait. In the meantime, they can revisit the world in this new novella, which follows 13 characters on their Threshing Days, when they endure a deadly trial in attempts to bond with a dragon. It was read by 26,000 users this week and has a 4.4 average rating.

The reigning queen of thrillers is back, this time with an October-appropriate story. After losing her job, Julia moves in with her elderly grandmother in their family’s 17th-century estate in Massachusetts. Soon, she begins to suspect the house is haunted by a woman executed for witchcraft in 1692. It was read by 30,000 users this week and has a 4.0 average rating.
A Court of Splintered Harmony (A Court of Thorns and Roses #6) by Sarah J. Maas

With more than triple the readership of the #2 book on this list, the latest A Court of Thorns and Roses book is by far the most popular book of the moment. It’s the first in the Valkyrie Cycle, following the Night Court as they face off against the return of Koschei the Deathless. The next book in the Valkyrie Cycle comes out in January. This one was read by 71,000 users this week and has a 3.8 average rating.
